Il these anceration mutate the list

L = [2,1,3,6,3,7,0] # do below in order
L.remove(2) → mutates L = [1,3,6,3,7,0]
L.remove(3) → mutates L = [1,6,3,7,0]
del(L[1]) → mutates L = [1,3,7,0]
L.pop() → returns 0 and mutates L = [1,3,7]
CONVERT LISTS TO STRINGS AND BACK
with list(s), returns a list with every character from s an element in L
split a string on a character
parameter, splits on spaces if called without a parameter
list of characters into a string
, can give a character in quotes to add char between every element

s = "I<3 cs"          → s is a string
list(s)                  → returns ['I', '<', '3', ' ', 'c', 's']
s.split('<')           → returns ['I', '3 cs']
L = ['a','b','c']  → L is a list
''.join(L)               → returns "abc"
''.join(L)               → returns "a_b_c"

L=[9, 6, 0, 3]
sorted(L)          → returns sorted list, does not mutate L
L.sort()           → mutates L=[0, 3, 6, 9]
L.reverse()      → mutates L=[9, 6, 3, 0]
